script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for December 20. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Howard Thurman said: Don't ask what the world needs.  Ask what makes you come alive—because what the world needs is people who have come alive.  Today we explore why this isn't selfish.

Your sense of aliveness is information. When you feel energized, engaged, and fully present, your brain is telling you: this matters to you. It's not frivolous—it's a compass pointing toward your unique contribution. Ignoring it is ignoring yourself. Psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi discovered that our happiest moments aren't passive or relaxing.  They happen when we're stretched in a meaningful challenge—what he called flow.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You don't find your aliveness by thinking about it.  You find it by noticing when you feel most like yourself.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Aliveness Inventory - Finding Your Fuel.

Here's your activity: Make a list of 5 moments from the past month when you felt most alive. Look for patterns: what were you doing, who were you with, what made it special? This helps you identify activities and contexts that generate energy and aliveness.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what makes you come alive can be applied to aliveness inventory - finding your fuel. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
